nodes.name: usb_uart_debug
nodes.description: CP2102N provides the USB-to-UART debug bridge for the main controller. It uses the external VIN_5V USB rail for USB presence and device power-related pins, and exposes a 3.3V-domain UART interface toward the ESP32. VIO must be tied to the system 3.3V rail so UART I/O levels match the MCU domain. USB D+ and D- terminate in this module as the USB data interface. Optional modem-control-assisted auto-program/reset intent may be supported through DTR and RTS routed to the MCU control module inputs, but exact polarity shaping is deferred to downstream wiring. Unused CP2102N status and GPIO pins remain uncommitted unless later needed.

nodes.name: battery_charger
nodes.description: TP4056 implements single-cell Li-ion charging from the external VIN_5V USB input into the battery positive node VBAT. This module owns the charger-to-battery energy flow and charge-current programming intent, but does not implement load-sharing or power-path ORing as explicitly excluded by the brief. The charger output goes directly to the battery cell side, while battery protection is handled downstream by the dedicated protection module. Any charger status indication or programming network is deferred to downstream wiring because no authoritative TP4056 pin list was provided here.

nodes.name: battery_protection
nodes.description: DW01A provides Li-ion cell protection between the raw battery node and the protected system battery rail. It monitors the cell at the VBAT side and controls the protected discharge/charge path so the rest of the system is powered only from the protected battery node. This module is the sole provider of the protected battery rail used by the regulator. The external back-to-back protection MOSFET path required by this IC is part of downstream implementation intent and must preserve the protection boundary between raw battery and system load.

nodes.name: power_3v3
nodes.description: ME6211 generates the regulated 3.3V system rail from the protected battery input. This module is the only provider of VCC_3V3 for the digital system. CE should be configured for an always-on policy unless a later system-level power-control requirement is introduced. The regulator input must come from the protected battery node, not directly from USB or the raw cell, to preserve the requested battery protection topology.

nodes.name: mcu
nodes.description: ESP32-WROOM-32E is the main controller for the IoT gateway. It runs from VCC_3V3, exposes the primary UART for debug communication with the USB-UART bridge, and exposes a shared I2C master bus for the environmental sensor. EN is the module reset/enable control input and IO0 is the boot strap input; these are also the natural targets for CP2102N-assisted auto-reset/boot sequencing through passive shaping if implemented later. Boot intent is normal flash boot in default operation, with IO0 only asserted for programming entry. This module owns I2C bus master role and should own shared-bus biasing policy so downstream wiring does not duplicate pull-ups elsewhere.

nodes.name: sensor_env
nodes.description: BME280 provides environmental sensing to the ESP32 over I2C. It is powered from VCC_3V3 on both VDD and VDDIO. CSB must be configured for I2C mode. SDO sets the I2C address selection and should be tied deterministically during downstream wiring; because the brief does not require a specific alternate address, either valid I2C address choice is acceptable as long as it is consistent with firmware. This module does not own I2C pull-ups; shared bus biasing should remain in the MCU side per system policy.
